course_title: Roles and Opportunities in Speech Pathology
course_description: This course introduces students to current and emerging roles and technologies associated with speech pathology practice. In this course, students engage in learning activities that foster skill development in planning, implementation and evaluation of speech pathology services.

course_aims:
Speech pathology is an evolving profession and speech pathologists fulfil a variety of roles across diverse contexts and communities. SPCH4113 presents students with real-life service delivery issues and aims to further develop students’ understanding of professional roles, ethical responsibilities, clinical reasoning and career development.

In SPCH4113, students will independently engage with online learning resources while having authentic learning experiences with peers and teaching staff in tutorials. Student participation is required in all learning activities. The format of the course provides more flexibility with learning, but the associated workload is similar to that of a traditional course.

learning_outcomes.description: Describe the roles and ethical responsibilities of speech pathologists across a range of professional contexts (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1 1.7, 2.1 2.7, 3.1 3.6).

Explain how current and emerging technologies are used to support speech pathology practice, including considerations of access, safety and professional responsibility (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1 1.3, 1.5, 1.7, 2.6, 3.2, 3.4 and 3.5).
Demonstrate professional communication skills and emerging professional identity in preparation for entering the speech pathology workforce (SPA PS Domains/Standards 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 3.6).
Apply foundational principles of problem-solving and innovation to identify potential contributions to speech pathology services and practice (SPA PS Domains/Standards 2.7, 3.4).
Work collaboratively in professional teams (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.4, 2.3, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.3, 3.4).

assessment_details.title: Employability Part A: Job Application Package
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment requires students to demonstrate understanding of the application process for a speech pathology role by preparing a professional application package. Students will respond to one (1) of three (3) job advertisements by writing a cover letter and answering selection criteria as specified in the advertisement. Students will also provide a mock LinkedIn profile that will be viewed by your prospective employer as part of the application process. A detailed task description and rubric will be provided on the SPCH4113 Blackboard site. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. assessment_details.task_description: Students will work in groups to present a 15 -minute Clinical Bite on "The Future of Speech Pathology". Each group will need to develop a persuasive, innovative, and engaging learning activity to inform the audience of how they perceive the future of speech pathology practice to look in a specific context. Each group will be allocated a different context to consider in their presentation. A detailed task description and rubric will be provided on the SPCH4113 Blackboard site. Students will be marked on both the quality and content of their presentation (20%) and a peer assessment on teamwork (5%). Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. When a student is required to complete an oral or practical assessment item worth 20% or more, the performance will be recorded and retained per Appendix 1 ( Assessment Procedure (95) ). assessment_details.title: Integrating Technology into Future Practice Video Assignment
assessment_details.task_description: The goal of this assignment is to encourage students to critically reflect on the role of technology in clinical settings and develop strategies for effectively integrating technological tools into their future practice. Students will create a 5-6 minute video presentation outlining how they plan to incorporate technology into their clinical work as a future speech-language pathologist. Students may use slides, screen recordings, and/or visual aids to enhance their presentation. A detailed task description and rubric will be provided on the SPCH4113 Blackboard site. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 5 (23 Feb - 29 Mar)
learning_activities.topic: Self-Directed Learning Students are required to access weekly content via Blackboard and complete the necessary learning activities prior to each tutorial. Content includes in depth exploration of roles and opportunities in different speech pathology contexts, factors impacting the profession both now and in the future (e.g., telepractice, technology and AI), and applying for jobs in speech pathology. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 5 (23 Feb - 29 Mar)
learning_activities.topic: Tutorials Students are required to attend two (2) tutorial sessions each week from Week 1 to Week 5. Each tutorial will be 2 hours in duration. These tutorials will focus on discussion and problem-solving specific to weekly content. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
